visual.slide: Cold smearing trades an O(sigma^3) error for negative weights
visual.issue: The MV occupation convention on this slide is the mirror image of the one in Quantum ESPRESSO, the code used for the runs (and, as far as I recall, of the MV paper). The slide uses x = (eps-mu)/sigma and f = integral from x to infinity, which gives 0.60 at mu and negative weights above mu. QE evaluates wgauss((E_F - eps)/degauss, -1) = 0.5*erf(y) + exp(-y^2)/sqrt(2*pi) + 0.5 with y = x - 1/sqrt2. In that form the weight is 0.40 at E_F, never negative, and peaks at 1.083 at sqrt2*sigma below E_F. The non-monotonic behaviour and the 0.083 excursion survive; the stated sign and side do not. The slide copies monograph M04 eq. mono-dft-mv and lines 199-208, so the error comes from the source. I could not check this here because QE source is not on the machine.
visual.evidence: 16_backup.tex lines 118-123 (f = int_x^inf delta, x = (eps-mu)/sigma) and line 142 ('0.60 at x = 0 ... minimum -0.083 at x = sqrt2: negative up to about 2 sigma above mu'). Title says 'negative weights'. M04_dft_theory.tex lines 199-208 say the same. QE Modules/wgauss.f90 (n = -1 branch) and gweights.f90 (argument (Ef - et)/degauss) use the opposite orientation.
visual.fix: Check this against QE Modules/wgauss.f90 and raise it with the monograph owner (M04). Until then, use wording that holds in either convention.
